name: Nitti
sources: Wikipedia — It's Goin' Down (Yung Joc song): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_Goin%27_Down_(Yung_Joc_song)
notes: ⛔ **The research names the parameter outright, and it is an unusual one: "this repetition-without-development is the parameter".** So this model is the only entry in the batch with `melody.endVariation` false and `emptyBarBias` 0 — the motif restates exactly, bar after bar, and never gets a closing variation. `phraseBars` weights 1 bar at 7:2, `contour.riff` is 0.96 and `octaveJumpProb` tops out at 0.04. Density is high because the research's words are "sharp, insistent keyboards" and "a maddeningly repetitive synth line": [5, 8] notes a bar of `staccato_piano_stab`, and the arrangement gives it a motif-alone intro, a motif-only breakdown and `dropOutBeats.prob` 0.35 — the lowest here, because "the motif never drops out". The kit is the lane's documented "clicking drumbeat": `rim` leading a three-lane perc block at −6 dB, `layerClapOffsetMs` [0, 2], and `velocityTiers` under the archetype's, because a popping click in place of a snare is a quiet event. ⚠ **Confidence is medium against the research's high-medium**; the inference is the tempo, whose 70–80 half-time band is marked [LOW-CONF on the number], so `session.bpm` 140–160 is a lane reading. His production and feature credits and the beat's elements are what is sourced. ⛔ **This is the same record as `yung-joc` seen from the desk, and the two are deliberately parameterised apart**: the artist's catalog varies at the phrase end and breathes; the producer's workflow does not. The separation is `endVariation`, `emptyBarBias`, `phraseBars` and `hihat.continuous`, and it is intentional rather than incidental. ⚠ The `i–VII` family at weight 4 is the research's "passing VII" and is sourced; nothing else in the chord block is, and its variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` [2, 11] rather than from progressions. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
